newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks closed down on Dow, rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks closed down on Dow, rate jitters.

text.p: Philippine shares closed down for the second straight session on Tuesday as investors were kept at bay by a weak Dow Jones index and fears over the U.S. Federal Reserve's meeting on interest rates, traders said.
"Investors just want to be liquid waiting for tomorrow's Fed results," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities.
The main index finished 22.37 points, or 0.72 percent, lower at 3,093.21 points.
The Fed's Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday (Wednesday in Manila) to decide on U.S. interest rates.
"People were trading on selective issues particularly those that have been battered in recent sessions such as Digitel and Piltel," Teresa Lee, assistant vice-president at Lippo Securities said.
Traders said bargain-hunting will likely take place on Wednesday, particularly on issues which have been laggards.
But Liboro said investors are unlikely to take long positions with Christmas holidays in the offing.
